newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey passes law for private thermal power plants.
newsitem.headline: Turkey passes law for private thermal power plants.

text.p: The Turkish presidency on Saturday approved a law that will enable private entities to build coal- and gas-fired power plants to produce electricity and sell it to the government, the Official Gazette said.
It said local and foreign private companies and consortia would benefit from the build-operate (BO) law, an offshoot to its parent build-operate-transfer (BOT) scheme.
Turkey tendered for six gas-fired power plants with a total capacity of 5,200 Megawatts in February to be built under the BO scheme.
But the Council of State, the top administrative court, suspended the tenders after legal objections by the Chamber of Electrical Engineers (EMO).
EMO said the scheme overruled the constitution by giving concessions to private and foreign entities in producing electricity, regarded as a strategic product.
The law, prepared by the former government that included Islamists and conservatives, will enable the Energy Ministry to carry on with the tenders of the six power plants, officials said.

"The ministry will now complete the tenders in one month from now at the latest," Ugur Dogan, energy ministry undersecretary, told Reuters. "The law will invalidate the court's suspension decision and other projects will also go ahead."
The BO law differs from its parent BOT in that the builders of power plants should provide for fuel and other inputs themselves and should own the plant.
The BOT suggests a transfer of operational rights and possession to the government after 15 or 20 years of operation. It is used only in building hydraulic, geothermal and nuclear power plants.
